catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 3 results from completed trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Week 182 results from the completed Phase 3 PaTHway Trial in adults with hypoparathyroidism were reported, demonstrating sustained efficacy and safety over 3.5 years. Outcomes included an 86% responder rate on a multi-component endpoint, normalized key serum and urine chemistries, improved kidney function and quality of life, and independence from active vitamin D and therapeutic calcium.
catalyst_text_evidence: COPENHAGEN, Denmark, 2026-06-13 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced Week 182 data from its completed Phase 3 PaTHway Trial showing that long-term treatment with TransCon PTH (palopegteriparatide) demonstrated sustained efficacy and safety in adults with hypoparathyroidism. Over the three-and-a-half-year duration of the trial, TransCon PTH replicated the systemic actions of endogenous PTH, with a balanced, beneficial impact on the main target organ systems – CNS, kidney, small intestine, and bone – as demonstrated by improved quality of life and normalized and stable urine calcium, serum calcium, serum phosphate, and bone mineral density. 86% of patients were responders for the multi-component endpoint of (1) serum calcium in the normal range, (2) taking no active vitamin D, and (3) taking ≤600 mg/day of calcium. Significant improvements in kidney function were maintained, with mean (SE) eGFR of 80.2 (1.8) mL/min/1.73 m2 at Week 182, reflecting a mean (SE) increase of 11.0 (1.4) mL/min/1.73 m2 from baseline. Mean 24-hour urine calcium decreased substantially, normalized within 26 weeks, and remained normal through Week 182. In the trial, TransCon PTH treatment was generally well-tolerated, with no new safety signals identified.

catalyst_text: Announced positive five year Phase 2 hypoparathyroidism results
detailed_catalyst_text: Week 266 results from the Phase 2 PaTH Forward trial in adults with hypoparathyroidism showed sustained efficacy and safety over five years. Data demonstrated high responder rates, normalized calcium metrics, improved kidney function and quality of life, and independence from active vitamin D and therapeutic calcium, supporting durable disease control.
catalyst_text_evidence: Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced 5-year (Week 266) data from its Phase 2 PaTH Forward Trial showing that long-term treatment with TransCon PTH (palopegteriparatide) demonstrated sustained efficacy and safety in adults with hypoparathyroidism. 82% of patients were responders for the multi-component endpoint of (1) serum calcium in the normal range, (2) taking no active vitamin D, and (3) taking <600 mg/day of calcium. Significant improvements in kidney function were maintained, with mean (SE) eGFR of 78.0 (3.0) mL/min/1.73 m2 at Week 266, reflecting a mean (SE) increase of 9.4 (1.9) mL/min/1.73 m2 from baseline. In the trial, TransCon PTH treatment was generally well-tolerated, with no new safety signals identified.

catalyst_text: Reported positive subgroup results from pivotal achondroplasia trial
detailed_catalyst_text: New subgroup analysis data from a pivotal trial in children aged ≥5 years with achondroplasia showed significantly greater annualized growth velocity versus placebo at Week 52, with improvements sustained through up to two years. Safety in this subgroup was favorable, with only mild injection site reactions, no symptomatic hypotension, and no acceleration of bone age, supporting potential for healthy, proportional growth.
catalyst_text_evidence: Ascendis Pharma A/S ... today announced new data from a subgroup analysis showing that children with achondroplasia ≥5 years of age at enrollment treated with once-weekly TransCon CNP (navepegritide) in its pivotal ApproaCH Trial demonstrated significantly greater annualized growth velocity (AGV) compared to placebo at Week 52, and sustained these growth improvements through up to two years of treatment. The safety profile for this subgroup through up to two years of treatment was similar to the overall population, with a low rate of injection site reactions (ISRs, all mild), no symptomatic hypotension, and no acceleration of bone age. ApproaCH was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial in 84 children with achondroplasia aged 2–11 years, investigating TransCon CNP (100 µg/kg once-weekly) versus placebo for 52 weeks, followed by a 52-week open-label extension (OLE) period in which all participants received TransCon CNP through Week 104.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 2 Week 52 combination data
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported Week 52 results from a Phase 2 open-label trial evaluating once-weekly combination therapy in children with achondroplasia. Data showed substantial improvements beyond linear growth, including increased arm span, larger spinal interpedicular distances, and improved tibial femoral angle, suggesting benefits in limb proportion, spinal canal dimensions, and leg alignment. All children completed 52 weeks of treatment and remained on therapy.
catalyst_text_evidence: COPENHAGEN, Denmark, 2026-04-08 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced new data demonstrating TransCon hGH accelerated TransCon CNP's benefits beyond linear growth with substantial improvements in arm span, spinal canal dimensions, and lower limb alignment. The new data are from Week 52 of the ongoing Phase 2 COACH Trial of combination therapy with once-weekly TransCon CNP and once-weekly TransCon hGH in children with achondroplasia. Unprecedented improvements in arm span observed at Week 52 with TransCon CNP and TransCon hGH combination therapy, a measure highly meaningful to the achondroplasia community, with the mean change from baseline in achondroplasia (ACH)-specific arm span Z-scores at Week 52 for TransCon CNP treatment-naïve and TransCon CNP-treated children in COACH were +1.02 and +0.66, respectively. Mean of L1-L5 average changes in interpedicular distance (IPD) for TransCon CNP treatment-naïve and TransCon CNP-treated children on combination therapy in COACH were +1.7 mm and +1.1 mm, respectively, compared to +0.6 mm for children on TransCon CNP monotherapy in ApproaCH. For the TransCon CNP treatment-naïve cohort, the mean change in tibial femoral angle (TFA) Z-score was -0.86 with combination therapy at Week 52 in COACH and was -0.47 for TransCon CNP monotherapy at Week 52 in ApproaCH, indicating enhanced straightening of the legs. All children completed 52 weeks of treatment and remain on therapy in COACH as of today.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Week 52 topline Phase 2 results
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive Week 52 topline data from a Phase 2 randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in prepubertal children with Turner syndrome showed annualized height velocity comparable to daily somatropin. Safety and tolerability were similar, with no SCFE and no discontinuations, supporting potential as a once-weekly alternative.
catalyst_text_evidence: COPENHAGEN, Denmark, 2026-03-17 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced positive Week 52 topline results from New InsiGHTS, its Phase 2 randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in the U.S. investigating the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of once-weekly TransCon hGH (lonapegsomatropin; U.S. FDA-approved for pediatric and adult growth hormone deficiency (GHD) and approved in other territories for pediatric GHD) compared to daily somatropin in prepubertal children with Turner syndrome. At Week 52, children treated with TransCon hGH demonstrated improved annualized height velocity (AHV) similar to daily somatropin, independent of starting dose, with an LS mean AHV of 9.05 cm/year for all TransCon hGH-treated children, compared to 9.04 cm/year for those treated with daily somatropin. In the trial, TransCon hGH demonstrated a safety and tolerability profile similar to daily somatropin through follow-up of up to 143 weeks. Adverse events (AEs) were mild to moderate in severity, with no AEs leading to discontinuation of study drug. There were no occurrences of slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE).

catalyst_text: Presented positive two year results from pivotal trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Week 104 results from the pivotal ApproaCH Trial in children with achondroplasia showed sustained increases in linear growth and further improvements in body proportionality during the second year. The therapy was generally well tolerated over two years with mostly mild or moderate adverse events and no discontinuations. These findings support durable efficacy and safety for once-weekly treatment in pediatric achondroplasia.
catalyst_text_evidence: Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced new data from its pivotal ApproaCH Trial showing that children with achondroplasia treated with once-weekly TransCon CNP (navepegritide) maintained consistent improvements in growth through Week 104, with further improvement in body proportionality during the second year of treatment. These and other results were shared in an oral presentation by Dr. Ravi Savarirayan, M.B.B.S., M.D., Murdoch Children's Research Institute (Australia), during ACMG 2026, the Annual Clinical Genetics Meeting held 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-14 in Baltimore, Maryland. Through two years of treatment, TransCon CNP was generally well-tolerated. Most adverse events in TransCon CNP-treated children were mild or moderate, with none leading to treatment discontinuation or withdrawal from the trial.

catalyst_text: Received FDA accelerated approval and rare pediatric voucher
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted accelerated approval for a once-weekly therapy to increase linear growth in children aged 2 years and older with achondroplasia and open epiphyses. Approval was supported by randomized, placebo-controlled trials and open-label extension data, with continued approval contingent on confirmatory studies. In connection with the approval, a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher was issued.
catalyst_text_evidence: Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced that the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) has granted approval under the FDA's Accelerated Approval Program for YUVIWEL (navepegritide; developed as TransCon CNP), the first and only once-weekly treatment indicated to increase linear growth in children 2 years of age and older with achondroplasia with open epiphyses. The FDA based its approval of YUVIWEL on their review of the clinical package for TransCon CNP submitted with the Company's New Drug Application, which included safety and efficacy data from three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials and up to three years of open-label extension data. With this approval, the FDA also issued a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV), which confers priority review to a subsequent drug application that would not otherwise qualify for priority review.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 2 Week 52 topline results
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline Week 52 results from the Phase 2 COACH trial of once-weekly combination therapy in children with achondroplasia showed durable growth, improvements in body proportionality and arm span, and a safety profile consistent with monotherapies. Children exceeded the 97th-percentile annualized growth velocity of average-stature peers, indicating additive efficacy versus monotherapy.
catalyst_text_evidence: COPENHAGEN, Denmark, 2026-01-08 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced topline results from Week 52 of COACH, the first Phase 2 clinical trial to evaluate combination therapy with once-weekly TransCon CNP (navepegritide) and once-weekly TransCon hGH (lonapegsomatropin) in children with achondroplasia. At Week 52, combination therapy showed durable growth without compromising safety or tolerability. In addition, combination therapy demonstrated benefits beyond linear growth with improvements in body proportionality and arm span, aligning with the increase in linear growth. All children completed 52 weeks of treatment and remain on therapy in COACH as of today.

catalyst_text: PDUFA date extended to February 28 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA deemed additional materials submitted on 2025-11-05 a major amendment to the NDA for children with achondroplasia, which extended the target action date to 2026-02-28. This confirms the review remains active and allows time to finalize the post‑marketing requirement protocol.
catalyst_text_evidence: Ascendis Pharma A/S (NASDAQ:ASND) today announced that the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) notified the Company that information submitted on 2025-11-05, related to the post-marketing requirement, in response to the FDA's ongoing review of the New Drug Application (NDA) for TransCon CNP (navepegritide) for children with achondroplasia, constituted a major amendment to the NDA. Accordingly, the FDA has extended the PDUFA target action date by three months to 2026-02-28.
